roles.name: OpenSSH server
roles.summary: Remote encrypted shell access, file transfer and tunnelling for administering the server.
roles.notes: The recommended way to administer Aether Server. The shipped drop-in forbids root login and pins a modern key exchange, but leaves password authentication on until you install a key.

roles.name: DHCP server
roles.summary: Dynamically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks, gateways and DNS servers to devices on a network.
roles.notes: Needs a subnet, an address pool and a static server address before it can hand out leases. Edit /etc/kea/kea-dhcp4.conf and validate with kea-dhcp4 -t.

roles.name: DNS server
roles.summary: Resolves names to addresses for the network and caches answers to speed up lookups.
roles.notes: Recursion is loopback-only in the shipped template. Declare authoritative zones in named.conf.local, or forward to upstream resolvers.

roles.name: NTP server
roles.summary: Synchronizes the internal clocks of all computers and devices on a network for precise, unified timekeeping.
roles.notes: Serves time to the local subnet and steps the clock on boot. Point upstream sources at your regional pool or an internal reference.

roles.name: AAA server (RADIUS / TACACS+)
roles.summary: Handles authentication, authorization and accounting (AAA) for users connecting to enterprise networks or VPNs.
roles.notes: FreeRADIUS covers 802.1X and VPN authentication; tac_plus covers legacy network equipment. Both start with a local shared secret you must change.

roles.name: Reverse proxy / load balancer
roles.summary: Terminates client connections and distributes them across backend servers, with health checks and TLS termination.
roles.notes: The example backend is a single placeholder host on port 8080. Add servers and health checks under the backend section.

roles.name: VPN server (WireGuard)
roles.summary: Offers an encrypted tunnel into the private network for remote users and site-to-site links.
roles.notes: The interface key and every peer key are placeholders. Generate them with wg genkey / wg pubkey and replace the private keys before enabling.

roles.name: Directory server (OpenLDAP)
roles.summary: Central user, group and policy directory for Unix and application authentication over LDAP.
roles.notes: Define your base DN and root credentials before starting slapd. For Kerberos-backed identity that Windows clients can join, use the AD-compatible domain controller role instead.

roles.name: Certificate authority
roles.summary: Issues and revokes X.509 certificates for the network so internal TLS does not depend on public CAs.
roles.notes: Run the initialisation once and treat the CA password and root key as production secrets. The shipped configuration exposes an ACME and JWK provisioner endpoint.

roles.name: AD-compatible domain controller (Samba AD DC)
roles.summary: Raises a new Active Directory-compatible domain that Windows and Linux clients can join.
roles.notes: Provision with samba-tool domain provision --use-rfc2307. Creating a new domain is irreversible and needs a static address and correct DNS. Do not enable this and the plain file server on the same machine without separating their roles.

roles.name: Central syslog server
roles.summary: Centrally collects, stores and logs event messages generated by routers, switches, firewalls and other endpoints.
roles.notes: Receives RFC 5424 over TCP and UDP and files logs per remote host under /var/log/remote. UDP is fire-and-forget; prefer TCP for point-to-point links.

roles.name: Monitoring and dashboards
roles.summary: Scrapes metrics from hosts and applications and presents them on alertable dashboards.
roles.notes: Prometheus scrapes this host and any targets you add; Grafana is the dashboard. Change Grafana's default administrator password on first sign-in.

roles.name: File server (Samba)
roles.summary: Provides centralised storage, sharing and permission management for files within a local network to Windows and Linux clients.
roles.notes: Shares a single /srv/aether share for an authenticated group by default. Set Samba passwords with smbpasswd -a and adjust the share path and access in smb.conf.

roles.name: Database server (PostgreSQL)
roles.summary: Hosts a relational database that processes complex queries and manages structured data for applications.
roles.notes: Listens on loopback by default. Open it to the network deliberately by changing listen_addresses and the host rule in pg_hba.conf, then reload the server.

roles.name: FTP server (vsftpd)
roles.summary: Allows file uploads and downloads between clients and the host using the File Transfer Protocol.
roles.notes: Plain FTP sends credentials in the clear. Where possible use the SFTP subsystem of the SSH server instead; TLS for FTP is available but off in this template.

roles.name: Backup server (restic REST)
roles.summary: Receives encrypted, deduplicated backups from Aether and restic clients over an authenticated HTTP endpoint.
roles.notes: Aether's client backup tooling already speaks restic. Set the repository password on the client; the server only stores ciphertext and never sees your data.

roles.name: Web server (Nginx)
roles.summary: Processes HTTP/HTTPS requests from browsers to deliver websites and static web content.
roles.notes: Serves /srv/www. Add a TLS server block and point the certificate path at the certificate-authority role or a public CA.

roles.name: Application server (PHP-FPM)
roles.summary: Runs the business logic and frameworks behind a web frontend rather than serving files directly.
roles.notes: The pool listens only on a local socket and never on the network. Pair it with the web server, which proxies matching requests to that socket.

roles.name: Mail server (Postfix + Dovecot)
roles.summary: Routes, delivers, sends and stores electronic mail using SMTP, IMAP and POP3.
roles.notes: Deliverability needs correct MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records plus a trusted TLS certificate, and many networks block outbound port 25. Configure an outbound relay if direct delivery is blocked.

roles.name: Proxy server (Squid)
roles.summary: Acts as an intermediary gateway between client devices and the internet for content filtering, caching and privacy.
roles.notes: Only the local subnet may use the proxy in the shipped template. Add ACLs to allow other networks and to block or allow categories of content.

roles.name: Git server (Gitea)
roles.summary: Hosts Git repositories with a web interface, issues, pull requests and an API for a team.
roles.notes: Runs as the gitea account against /var/lib/gitea. Complete first-run setup in the browser and change the database credentials if you attach one.

roles.name: Virtualization host (libvirt / KVM)
roles.summary: Runs hypervisor software that splits a single physical machine into isolated virtual servers.
roles.notes: Needs hardware virtualisation (VT-x/AMD-V) enabled in firmware. Guest traffic is left to per-network libvirt rules rather than opened globally.

roles.name: Container host (Podman)
roles.summary: Runs OCI containers and pods as rootless or system services without a long-running daemon.
roles.notes: Ships a minimal container configuration and enables the API socket. Container ports are published explicitly per container rather than opened host-wide.

roles.name: Print server (CUPS)
roles.summary: Manages network print queues, routing print jobs from computers to physical office printers.
roles.notes: Shares printers with the local subnet and enables the web administration interface on loopback. Add printers with lpadmin or the web interface.

roles.name: VoIP / PBX server (Asterisk)
roles.summary: Provides IP telephony: registrations, call routing, voicemail and conferencing for desk and soft phones.
roles.notes: Registers a single example endpoint. RTP media uses a UDP port range, which must be opened separately for calls to carry audio.

roles.name: Media streaming server (Jellyfin)
roles.summary: Streams video, audio and photos to browsers, phones and televisions from the server's own storage.
roles.notes: Complete first-run setup in the browser, then point libraries at your media directories. Hardware transcoding needs extra firmware and a supported GPU.

roles.name: CI/CD runner (GitLab Runner)
roles.summary: Executes automated build, test and deployment jobs registered to a GitLab instance.
roles.notes: Unregistered in this template. Register with gitlab-runner register and choose an executor deliberately; a shell executor gives jobs the runner account's full access.
